GTA 6 PS5 Codes Potentially Being Stolen from Physical Copies Using Flashlight Trick

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (313 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A potentially problematic manufacturing oversight may be resulting in some GTA 6 codes being stolen from retail PS5 cases.
  • Some reports claim that by pointing a strong flashlight at the side of the case, it’s possible to shine light into the empty Blu-ray box in such a way that it makes the code printed on the insert visible.
  • Remember, GTA 6’s physical release is a code-in-box, and doesn’t have a Blu-ray disc.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A potentially problematic manufacturing oversight may be resulting in some GTA 6 codes being stolen from retail PS5 cases.

Some reports claim that by pointing a strong flashlight at the side of the case, it’s possible to shine light into the empty Blu-ray box in such a way that it makes the code printed on the insert visible.

Remember, GTA 6’s physical release is a code-in-box, and doesn’t have a Blu-ray disc.

There is some debate about whether the included poster insert blocks the light and makes this impossible; some say they’ve been able to replicate the issue, while others say it can’t be done with a sealed copy.

It has been revealed that it’s also worth noting that the US release specifically has a camouflaged pattern around the code, as shown by ResetEra user Mattmo831. That means you can certainly shine light into the box, but you can’t read the code on the other side.

Some PEGI units don’t have the camouflage pattern, so technically the code is visible using this trick, although again there’s still debate over whether the poster blocks the light in sealed copies.

It’s worth pointing out that codes aren’t activated at the point of purchase like other digital vouchers, so assuming the flashlight method works, it would be perfectly possible to pilfer a working copy of the game.

I think this story will explode if it turns out to be true, but it all just depends on how many PEGI copies don’t have the camouflage pattern and whether the inserted poster blocks the light or not.

As far as I can see, there aren’t an enormous number of people who’ve complained upon buying the physical version that their code has been redeemed – but if this method works, the publicity around it will now surely see the probability increase.

[source reddit.com, via resetera.com].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Industry observers note that alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

According to recent reports, sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

According to recent reports, the Pokemon Trading Card Game's latest expansion, Delta Reign, has been available for around 10 days now. The Rayquaza-themed set is one of this year's best and features a handful of very cool, very expensive cards.

Now that the dust has begun to settle and the prices have started to stabilize, here are the ten most expensive cards that you can pull (or buy) from the Pokemon TCG's Delta Reign expansion.

I like this Groudon card a lot. 2026 has been a bit of a tepid year for Illustration Rares, but this is up there with the best. I'll stand by the fact that it's a shame that Groudon, Kyogre, and Rayquaza didn't all get Special Illustration Rares, but it's a nice card.

At $20, it won't break the bank, but having any Groudon card is going to be relatively pricey, and so it's made its way onto this list.

It has been revealed that shimaris Yukichi is one of the Pokemon Trading Card Game's most interesting upcoming artists. Their cutesy style has been a hit with fans, with the Team Rocket's Meowth and Dwebble Illustration Rares two of their best so far.

Recent findings suggest that they've now been entrusted with a Special Illustration Rare, and I love it. It has shades of Toshinao Aoki​​​​​​'s Lana's Aid card from Twilight Masquerade, and is well worth the $21.18 it's presently selling for.

According to recent reports, this Eevee card, along with Delta Reign's Zorua and Sprigatito Illustration Rares, was first released in Japan as one of three different decks. It's now made its way to the English-language Pokemon TCG, and it's a cutie.

I'm surprised this one is so cheap at just $21.84, because Eevee cards usually command a premium, and for a card this cute, that seems like a steal.

Mega Golisopod ex's Special Illustration Rare is one of Delta Reign's most disappointing cards, and typically the one SIR I've pulled from the set. It honestly just looks like a Full Art and features a Pokemon that isn't particularly popular.

Sources indicate that it does have the SIR tax, though, and it's at the moment selling for just shy of $24. It's not particularly playable, so it's a miracle it's as much as that.

Another underwhelming Special Illustration Rare is up next with Mega Golurk ex. It's certainly better than Mega Golisopod ex, with the towering golem standing in among ancient ruins, but I'd categorize it as okay.

It is the first card to break the $25 mark in the expansion, and that's in part because it's seeing some play in the competitive scene.

Sources indicate that when I was researching and putting together this list, the Kecleon Illustration Rare's price surprised me. Being illustrated by Tomokazu Komiya definitely helps, with their signature psychedelic style, but it's Kecleon.

I'd have expected the cutesy Growlithe, Sprigatito, and Zorua cards to be worth more, but this clearly shows how much people value an artist's work, with Kecleon sitting at $34.99.

It has been revealed that this card is very cool. I'm a big lover of Full Art trainer cards, and this epitomizes everything that's good about them. Zinnia is a bit of a fan favorite, and seeing her sitting on a rock, probably awaiting the return of Rayquaza, is iconic.

The price, $36.18, is fair for the card, especially as it's seeing action in competitive play. In decks that require a lot of energy, Zinnia's Trust's ability to move them around is very useful.

We're now into the substantial money, and this is my favorite card of the entire expansion. Raikou's Special Illustration Rare features the Legendary Beast bounding down a mountain with sparks flying. Whether by design or not, it looks like it's set in the same region as Zinnia's Trust.

At over $127, Raikou ex costs a pretty penny, but when all is said and done, it's likely to be one of the best cards to come out of the entire Mega Evolution era.

The Mega Hyper Rares are divisive. They're an interesting latest take on the Sword and Shield era's Gold cards, but it's hard to think they don't look a little tacky. This Mega Rayquaza ex, though, might be the best one released so far.

It's a Mega Hyper Rare, so it's always going to fetch a pretty penny, and when you throw in one of the TCG's most desirable Pokemon, you get the $221.55 price tag that this is presently selling for.

My price prediction for this card may have been off the mark, but the Mega Rayquaza ex Special Illustration Rare is unsurprisingly Delta Reign's premium card, reaching a few pennies over $300.

It has been revealed that it's illustrated by 2024 Illustration Contest winner Kazuki Minami, and it's one of the most uniquely styled cards the TCG has ever seen. I can't even begin to describe what is being depicted, but the giant green Mega Rayquaza, contrasted by the orange and yellow backdrop, is a sight to behold.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In what feels a fairly cheeky move during a time when memory shortages have infamously made it pretty much impossible to buy a decently powerful new graphics card without spending approximately a gazillion pounds/dollars/dollarpounds, Nvidia have decided to put out a Steam demo that allows folks to re-live the feeling of unboxing a ludicrously expensive graphics card in 2006.

According to recent reports, the demo, dubbed GeForce 8800 GTX - 20 Years of a Legend, has been developed by Dylan Browne. He previously made Through The Ages, a "real-time high end graphical cinematic that takes us on a nostalgic journey through three of NVIDIA's iconic GPUs" which is also on Steam for reasons.

Sources indicate that the GeForce 8800 GTX demo, as you might've guessed, is a tribute to that specific card in the form of a tech demo simulating what it was like to unbox one in a mid-2000s bedroom. Seriously, there's a copy of Crysis on the desk so you know this is the domain of a true devotee to the best graphics available in around 2007.

Industry observers note that "Step into a 2006-era PC gaming room, unbox the GeForce 8800 GTX, inspect it up close, and install it in an era-accurate PC tower," the demo's description declares. "Explore nods to GeForce history and hidden easter eggs as DLSS 4.5 with Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, Ray Reconstruction, path tracing, and Mega Geometry bring the nostalgic setting to life. From holding the card to the glow of the monitor, rediscover a moment in PC gaming history - or experience it for the first time!".

As the GeForce 8800 GTX was a top-line card that cost $599 on release in 2006 - about $1,000 in today's money if the online inflation calculator I've just used is on the money - this isn't really a 'we know cards are ludicrously expensive right now, but here's a reminder of when you used to be able to actually afford to unbox one' sort of demo. It is at least a free way to virtually experience having blown a chunk of your savings on something that can render really sexy textures without the existential dread of doing so in real life.

In a recent development, well, I say that, I've just noticed the minimum requirements for the demo note that you'll need an RTX 4070 card. So, depending on your current setup, this might well be a case of Nvidia offering the chance to render unboxing a card you couldn't afford in 2006 via a card you can't afford in 2026.

According to recent reports, is that about the best we can all hope for in 2026? Probably.

Crimson Desert PC specs don't keep resolution and framerate targets a secret, and they don't use upscaling for everything either

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game.
  • The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.
  • Recent findings suggest that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

Recent findings suggest that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

In a recent development, it’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

Sources indicate that and, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that here at Pure Xbox, we're rather stoked about Playground Games' revival of Fable.
  • So, let it been known for the record, I fully expect Fable to be a brilliant RPG.
  • In a recent development, the footage was revealed during Seattle FanFest as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary jollies, although most of it was stuff we'd sorta seen before, and the choice of location was questionable at best.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that here at Pure Xbox, we're rather stoked about Playground Games' revival of Fable. We were picking jaws up off the floor in June, then again at gamescom in August, and even left London FanFest feeling pretty jazzed with what we got to play of the upcoming RPG.

So, let it been known for the record, I fully expect Fable to be a brilliant RPG. Top class in execution, full of joy and wow moments aplenty, but what on earth was Xbox thinking promoting Fable with that four-minute gameplay video? C'mon gang!

In a recent development, the footage was revealed during Seattle FanFest as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary jollies, although most of it was stuff we'd sorta seen before, and the choice of location was questionable at best. See for yourself in the video above.

"Both myself and Craig had a chance to play this demo last weekend, and we both came away pretty darn impressed with what we'd played. That noted, we also remarked to each other that we wished we'd had a chance to explore Albion and interact with NPCs, which is something we'll have to wait a little bit longer for.".

Recent findings suggest that where we'd previously been gobsmacked by vibrant castle towns and lush wilderness, this latest setting felt rather basic and lacking in character or detail. It was just some generic cliffside. It's not necessarily bad, but it's hardly the sort of environment I'd think to stuff into a trailer meant to turn people onto Fable.

As the video goes on, we get a little combat featuring swords, archery, and a sprinkling of magic. It all looks good, and having played the combat myself, it feels fun. But it doesn't last long, nor does it show us anything upcoming or particularly interesting. The quest itself is cut short and lacking, as though it's just been ripped from a spoiler-free section of the game.

It has been revealed that just to reiterate, I reckon Fable will come good. Every gameplay reveal up until this point has been great. Massive fan. This one just feels a little odd, almost as if it was cobbled together last minute. That's not ideal when you're trying to convince players to pick up Fable when it rolls out on Xbox Series X|S, PC, and PS5 on February 23, 2027.

What do you make of the footage? Are we being too harsh, or is it a little lacklustre? Tell us your thoughts in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that over a decade ago, Hugh Jackman outlined his dream crossover between X-Men and Avengers. Now, Avengers: Doomsday is going to do right by that idea – and bring home 25 years of history between those characters.

"You see interviews of Hugh Jackman 15, 20 years ago saying, ‘People say it’s impossible, but maybe someday the X-Men and the Avengers can all get together,'" Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige told Empire. "It just felt right. It just felt like the fun way to culminate a quarter-century of storytelling.".

When doing press for 2013's The Wolverine, Jackman mentioned on multiple occasions that he would love to go claw-to-claw with The Avengers.

Recent findings suggest that at the time, he told Slash Film, "I actually just asked the other day, I said, 'I don't know what the legal situation is, but why don't these companies come together? Why isn't it possible?' Because personally, I would love to mix it up with Robert Downey Jr. and Iron Man and kick his ass.".

For now, Hugh Jackman isn't officially part of Doomsday – though, curiously, has a writing credit alongside Ryan Reynolds, which partially suggests Deadpool and Wolverine will factor in somehow.

In a recent development, but there are plenty of X-Men to make up for it, including James Marsden's Cyclops, Sir Ian McKellen's Magneto, and the late Patrick Stewart reprising his Professor Charles Xavier role once more. Channing Tatum's Gambit is also featured, but with a slightly different accent to his incomprehensible Cajun drawl that was played for laughs in Deadpool and Wolverine.

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and worldwide on December 18.

For more, we have a guide on how to watch the X-Men movies in order, as well as the complete Marvel timeline to look back on.

In a recent development, no doubt eager as peas to help pay off EA's billions in debt, battle royale shooter Apex Legends is set to run another of its intellectual propertytastic crossover events. This one, starting on November 10th, stars Godzilla, of Godzilla Minus Zero, Godzilla vs. Kong, Godzilla (1954), Godzilla 2000: Millennium, Godzilla (1998), Son of Godzilla, and Godzilla (2014). I might be missing some.

In a recent development, besides a profitable range of weapon and character skins, most of which appear to have hot glue gunned an 70-year film franchise's worth of dorsal fins all over themselves, the King of the Monsters himself will show up on the game's Storm Point map. He does at least have more than a background cameo: he'll occasionally blast an area with Legend-melting atomic breath, though brave souls who risk the danger zone can score a custom Devotion LMG with a unique heat ray attack of its own.

It has been revealed that worth noting also that the character skins are each based on a certain 'zilla movie, though as our freelance news writer and associate Large Lizard Cinema expert Ashley isn't working today, I'm not sure which of these are from hits and which are the duds. Walking wallhack motherfucker Bloodhound gets the newest fashion, their skin being inspired by Minus Zero, while my personal favourite Scottish scientist Horizon gets duds based on Massive G in Godzilla vs. Destoroyah. Octane's skin is taken from... something called a Jet Jaguar? Google suggests this may in fact be elite Godzilla knowledge, something I clearly lack.

It has been revealed that regardless, and with the understanding that a lot of effort goes into these crossovers, I still kinda wish they didn't exist? Even putting aside basic game-playing problems with how, for example, wacky skins interfere with Legend silhouettes – you couldn't pay me to initiate a fight against a full team of near-identical Gundampeople - it's just icky to have an otherwise sharp, smart, at times fiercely competitive battle royale turned into an animated billboard for a few days.

In a recent development, besides, Apex already has its own kaiju: the sleepy, pacifist Leviathans that innocently wandered into the King's Canyon map for a few of the earlier seasons. I consider these much better Friend Material than Godzilla, on the grounds that they'd only kill you by accident, and it was usually your own fault - by wandering under their briefly raised megahooves - anyway.

Recent findings suggest that another day, another opportunity for some horsing around! I'm being literal here, to be clear, as a latest update for The Legend of Khiimori dropped yesterday. It's called The Mongolian Expanse, opening up the map a whole lot more and making a sweep of other additions to the game.

Previously, you might have looked out unto the snowy mountainscapes and the scorching deserts and thought "boy howdy am I glad I can't go there, those temperatures look like a nightmare to deal with!" Well, good news, as you now can head to those locales, each with "their own waystations, Yam nodes, named places, chests and bandit caches.".

According to recent reports, you don't want to wander there without some amount of prep, however, as the mountains are cold and difficult to climb, with wolves none too kind to humans like you. The desert, of course, is really hot, for both you and your horse. Both additions remind me of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and its use of extreme temperatures acting as a sort of challenge gate. Neat stuff!

The buck doesn't stop there with this update though. You'll find a whole host of new wildlife, ranging from wild boars, to gobi bears and camels. Of course, a horse game wouldn't be one without more horse, which there is! It's a new breed called the Marwari, a horse that is "built for endurance and especially resistant to heat, a strong partner for long, punishing Desert crossings." Beyond that, you'll also find more than 60 new horse skills, all findable across specific regions and for specific breeds.

Recent findings suggest that it's a nice beefy update with plenty more tweaks, additions and fixes on top of everything mentioned above. When it comes to the mountains and desert, you can also expect some massive additions there, as this is only the first part of this update. You can read about everything else the update offers right here on Steam.

The Humblers Awaken will launch on 1st December 2026 and brings a fresh adventure to the action-RPG with newly introduced quests, unexplored environments, colourful cosmetics and an expanded arsenal of gear. Here's a bit more about what you can expect:.

In a recent development, "The Sift is in danger once more, and the humblers – an ancient threat that has slumbered for ages – are beginning to wake up. Alongside this DLC will be a bonus free update - this will add new challenges, more weapons and armour to Minecraft II. It will also reunite heroes from the original Minecraft Dungeons (Hal, Hex, Adrienne and Valorie) as player skins. There'll also be the new trial dungeons, where you can earn powerful gear:.

"Take on the new trial dungeons to earn powerful gear. Available through Brave Haven, trial dungeons offer daily and weekly challenges that feature a combination of rule-bending modifiers and increased difficulty. Enormous spiders, constant TNT explosions, and soul projectiles are just some of the modifiers you will encounter in these dungeons!".

Last but not least, it's been confirmed the DLC 'Illusions of Grandeur' will launch at some point in Spring 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • Sources indicate that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

Sources indicate that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a newly introduced Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

In a recent development, once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the fresh Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

In a recent development, all-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

According to recent reports, casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

In a recent development, the most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

In a recent development, this is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a significant new upgrade - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that jason Ronald – vice president of Xbox's gaming devices and ecosystem team – has spoken in more detail about what Project Helix actually is. Namely, it doesn't sound like it's a Steam Machine.

Industry observers note that to celebrate the 25th anniversary since the original Xbox was released and Halo arrived in our lives (and almost 26 since The Rock revealed the console), Microsoft has released a magazine about the platform online. While a lot of it is about the history of the console, some details about the future of Xbox are sprinkled in there, with news about future releases like Fable, and a hint that there's maybe something going on with games like Crash Bandicoot and Tony Hawk. But the most significant bit of info is some more details about what Project Helix is.

Ronald – who Microsoft describes as the vice president of next generation – notes "it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," while touting its backwards compatibility capabilities, mentioning that he's "able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly.".

Industry observers note that he also speaks about removing "the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games," while explaining more about what Project Helix's rumored PC connection actually is. "We're very clear on the design goal" Ronald explains, "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games.".

Sources indicate that of course, the real question is how all-encompassing is the PC integration going to be. Presumably the Xbox Store is a sure bet, and probably Battle.net too. But the idea of having your Steam library available on console would be a pretty unassailable win for the console, but sadly I really don't see that happening in the age of Steam Machines.

Xbox Project Helix console could cost as much as $1,800 and is reportedly set to launch by Christmas 2028.

Remember DokeV? The bizarre Pokémon-esque game confirmed over five years ago from Pearl Abyss? The developer has gone on to make Crimson Desert, but in a upcoming financial report, it's shared its wild take on Pokémon is still coming.

Now its Charting the Unknown expansion for Crimson Desert is out, it's shifting more of its developers onto DokeV, and the firm is targeting a launch in the second half of 2028. Before the end of this year, however, it aims to reveal its latest "development progress".

DokeV was originally revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live in 2021, a show run by Geoff Keighley. There is a good chance the re-reveal of the game will take place next month at The Game Awards, then.

Here's that wacky announcement trailer as a reminder:.

Recent findings suggest that having shown it again, Pearl Abyss will have hands-on demos in the second half of 2027. It noted: "We will continue to communicate with players by sharing updates at optimal timing to effectively highlight the game's direction and core strengths.".

The problem is it sounds like the developer is embracing more AI development to achieve that.

Recent findings suggest that in the financial report, Pearl Abyss confirms that it's "integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality". AI is being used across "the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimisation", and its use is being expanded to the team's "entire development pipeline".

"This enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed," it added.

Industry observers note that for now, though, the studio claims AI serves "strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity". Humans are still behind the "core gameplay experience and actual content creation".

Recent findings suggest that crimson Desert got into hot water shortly after its release for including AI portraits in some of its environments. It did remove them from the game and issued an apology where it said the assets were "unintentionally included in the final release. This is not in line with our internal standards, and we take full responsibility for it.".

Now, as it looks to the future, Pearl Abyss seemingly plans to lean even more into AI development.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

According to recent reports, as everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the massive focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

Recent findings suggest that the event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot newly introduced arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

It has been revealed that in combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

Sources indicate that if he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Lord almighty, video games take a while to make, 'ey? Especially if you're just one person working on it by yourself. Such is the case with Faraway, out today, an arcade game that reminds me of the early days of PS3 indies "about a shooting star that creates constellations to stay alive," all made single-handedly by creator of cult-classic mobile game Eliss, Steph Thirion. Did I mention that Faraway took 16 years to make? Like I said, game development is a lengthy process.

Recent findings suggest that looking at Faraway, and knowing how long it took to produce, it doesn't surprise me to come from a dev who managed to release a mobile game in the early days of the platform, long before free-to-play got its chokehold on the industry. It also really does feel like it should be sitting amongst the likes of PixelJunk, this thing should be something I'm desperate to play on my PS3 while I wait for my controller to charge.

Sources indicate that as mentioned, you are a shooting star, a "spark meant to shine and vanish in a blink." But still you persist, connecting to and wrapping yourself around starts to "harvest their energy," in turn lengthening your own life, and of course, in arcadey fashion, racking up a nice score. It looks like game design as poetry, everything you're looking at procedurally generated to bring freshness to every run. I can fully envision this as a "one more run" kind of arcade game, the best kind, especially in an age long past the need to shove in another of your hard earned coins.

It has been revealed that faraway conceptually charms me because it taps into a style of game we don't get to see much of any more. What I'm saying is, I'm just a teensy bit sick of how many roguelikes there are, but that doesn't mean I don't want a game I can just hop in and out of at my own whims. Sure, arcade games might not be in vogue, I just miss them a bit. In any case, Faraway is available to pick up on Steam right now. Seems like it'll be worth a punt!

  • In a recent development, if you've not been using the Zelda Notes app while playing the Ocarina of Time remake, this is your sign to start.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been out for just over a week, and player stats prove that I'm not the only one who's died a few too many times to a ReDead. Solidarity.

In a recent development, if you've not been using the Zelda Notes app while playing the Ocarina of Time remake, this is your sign to start. Found within the Nintendo Switch App, its compatibility with the newly introduced remake is incredible if you're keen to track down all the secrets available, with an interactive map showing your completion in each area, if you're missing any Gold Skulltalas or Pieces of Heart, and more. Even if you want to go through the remake without a guide, though, it's still worth it just to have a peek at your player stats and see how they compare to everyone else's.

In a recent development, as highlighted by GoNintendo, the first week or so of Ocarina of Time remake stats in Zelda Notes' Global Play Data section are pretty interesting. Skulltalas are the most commonly defeated enemy, while the ever-horrifying ReDead and Gibdos are responsible for 18% of all deaths in the remake. I can't say that's surprising – they've always been a pain to deal with (as well as being utterly terrifying), but now we just have the stats to prove it.

Amusingly, tied with the hard-hitting Iron Knuckles for 7% of all deaths each, the runner-up here is, simply, fire. Sounds like a few too many people got overconfident when exploring Death Mountain without the Goron tunic. Please, stop setting poor Link on fire, folks.

A lot of stats here are still obviously being influenced by the enormous number of people who are only just diving into the game. Most people, for example, have only traveled around 1 kilometer in Hyrule, as opposed to a much smaller number who've already passed 200km. Some stats are more indicative of a longer playtime, though – the majority of folks are apparently professional gardeners, with over 1,000 pieces of grass cut, and 40% of people's most-used form of magic being the Lenses of Truth is almost certainly thanks to the group who've been through the Shadow Temple already.

The Zelda Notes app also tracks your time to clear the game – at 26 hours, I fall into the "20 hours+" category, which is the most common result, but some folks were very quick, coming in at just over 10 hours, instead.

In a recent development, if there's one thing these stats prove though, it's that more of you need to go fishing. The average, by quite a margin, is just one to four fish caught – we've got to get those numbers up. Now, if only the app could somehow track how many people got stuck in the Water Temple, too.

Be sure to check out our Ocarina of Time remake review to see what makes Nintendo's latest so special.

It has been revealed that "Bill: Seeing an image of a library with Fable 3 having a disc to digital badge. Error, or......".

Original Story: Yesterday, Xbox starting rolling out three fresh console features for Xbox Insiders to try out: rotating home backgrounds, the ability to choose which side the Xbox guide pops open on, and new ways to organise disc to digital games.

Recent findings suggest that they're all cool features that we're definitely keen to play around with, but what got our attention most was the image Xbox used to show off the fresh disc to digital patch. Particularly, the games featured with the D2D licence icon plopped in the bottom-left corner of each game tile.

According to recent reports, did Xbox just tease the inclusion of Xbox 360 games in the D2D programme? Well, that would be true if the image depicting Fable III is to be taken at face value. At a glance, you'd probably see the image above and think, 'great, that's awesome', but the more you look at it, the weirder it gets.

Avowed famously debuted on Xbox without a physical disc. So, if the theory about Xbox 360 games joining the programme is on the money, does that mean we're getting a physical copy of Avowed too? And what about Age of Empires IV? That never received a physical release either. Then If we really want to go Enola Holmes on this image, Forza games aren't D2D compatible.

We're thinking someone at Xbox might've messed up with this image. Announcements of this magnitude shouldn't be buried in an Xbox Insider update. Xbox should be shouting about it on the front page. So, why do an Xbox 360 game and two digital-only titles have D2D icons attached to them? I could think of a lazy reason.

Only time will tell, but consider us sceptical for now. We've chalked this one up to a blunder from Xbox, although it wouldn't surprise us if Xbox 360 games did eventually join the D2D programme. And hey, it's Xbox's birthday this Sunday. Maybe there's more to this than meets the eye.

Sometimes, you come across a game and instantly know it's for the sickos. Today that is Ablahshikar, a "turn-based salvage-survival CRPG adrift on the Candle Sea" where you rip out the organs of enemy warships to "rebuild your vessel into a doomed chimera," that is out now in early access. To be honest I could have just called it a CRPG and still labelled it as a game for sickos, yet everything that's going on here is obviously just doubling down on the sick factor.

Sources indicate that ablahshikar is a particular flavour of maximalism. Having not played it, it feels a bit impossible describe, I mean, just have a read of some of the game's Steam page: "Lo, destiny crooks a finger only to those whose eyes peer beyond þe next tempest. Take custody of a faltering war-barge that wanders the outer brine of Dastgerd. Thy wrists y-braced to a wan terminal of bone-whyte and tarnysshed latoun, þou steerest Ablahshikar by murke point-nettes and sputteryng tables." I don't know what any of that means! And I love it. Reminds me of Hylics in that the game's world is not translating itself for its audience; you take what you're given, and you figure it out yourself.

Judging from trailers and screenshots, there's a mix of activities to be getting on with. Occasionally you'll be piloting a strange, not alien, but definitely ancient ship of some kind in an arcadey sort of fashion. Then occasionally there's something that resembles Caves of Qud, i.e. some odd, 2D maybe dungeon crawling where your moves are dictated by individual keys on your keyboard. Then there's Disco Elysiumy cutscenes that feel like a video game designed in the year 1200 by someone from the year 2200, aesthetically anyway. As I said, it is a particular flavour of maximalism.

According to recent reports, truthfully, I do not know if I am sicko enough for Ablahshikar. Its mighty vision is terrifying, but I certainly am curious about it. Right now it's less than a fiver, and it'll only be in early access for roughly a couple of months where the price will then go up, so perhaps it's best to get in at the ground floor. If you are one such sicko, then you can pick it up on Steam right here.

All of the 6 finalists had some really great and unique ideas, and the entire dev team has been very impressed and amazed at the amount of creativity on display.

It wasn't easy picking a winner, but we ended up deciding on Cleanser Man due to his whimsical motif and unique color pattern.

The lid part on the detergent has a very Mega Man-esque design to it, and we like that the detergent itself is very colorful as well.

You have to be careful not to introduce too many elements to prevent the design from becoming too cluttered, so we like that the artist kept things relatively simple.

But there's still enough detail to it to give it that genuine Mega Man feel.

Once again, thank you to everyone who joined in the contest.

We really appreciate the time and effort everyone put into this.

And here's a look at Cleanser Man. Be sure to check out the video above to see it in action:.

In a recent development, mega Man: Dual Override is scheduled to release on Switch and Switch 2 in Spring 2027. So far, five Robot Masters have been unveiled, including Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, Cook Man, and the prize-winning Cleanser Man.   • As reported by Deadline, Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie will be helming a documentary about the beloved RPG studio for Canada's Super Channel.
  • Some big names from BioWare's history will be appearing in the doc, including its founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip, alongside the likes of longtime devs like Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It feels like every single week for the past few years has been the infinitely quotable 30 Rock quote on repeat. That feeling struck particularly last month when EA decided to shut down the iconic Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare. That obviously resulted in the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, of which a leaked trailer and some, now former, devs made sound pretty interesting. But hey! At least there's a documentary coming next year all about the studio that managed to capture the studio's last days! Yeah, I'm not so convinced by this upside either.

As reported by Deadline, Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie will be helming a documentary about the beloved RPG studio for Canada's Super Channel. It's called, punnily enough, Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, and will apparently take a look at its origins in 1995 all the way up to its closure and a bit beyond, planned for release in 2027. Filming began two years ago, so clearly this was meant to be much more of a celebratory project than the funeral procession it's going to be.

Some big names from BioWare's history will be appearing in the doc, including its founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip, alongside the likes of longtime devs like Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone. You can also expect appearances from Jennifer Hale, Casey Hudson and, as if his sole goal is to haunt this industry everywhere, Geoff Keighley.

In a statement, co-founders Muzyka and Zeschuk said, "When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved. BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again.".

Obviously the documentary won't only be about the studio's closure, it sounds like a much bigger effort than that, so hopefully it will be a way to recognise how much of an influence BioWare has had on RPGs. It's just a ridiculous shame that it's something of a posthumous release. Continued solidarity with all those at BioWare.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major upgrade arrives March 24, adding two upcoming Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Recent findings suggest that most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A massive challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier swiftly.

Recent findings suggest that our first newly introduced arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

Industry observers note that the other fresh Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Sources indicate that being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Recent findings suggest that outside of all the very crucial action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever introduces several fresh features, including a camping system that provides useful buffs to help you explore Azeroth. One of the first quests you'll encounter that uses this system is The Great Outdoors, a short introduction to camping. If you've landed on this guide, I'm sure you may be looking for some extra help here.

Although the quest seems straightforward, I found that one objective doesn't always register properly. If you're having the same problem, here's how to complete the quest and get around the glitch. We detail everything you need to know, below.

Industry observers note that you can start The Great Outdoors early in your adventure, regardless of your race. The quest giver and location vary by starting area, but the objectives remain the same.

Here's how to complete The Great Outdoors:.

While resting, you'll see the Welcoming Campfire effect counting down. Once the timer finishes, you'll receive Boosted Rest and complete the main objective.

When completing The Great Outdoors, I found that the Sit near campfire objective didn't always register, even when I was sitting beside the correct fire.

Recent findings suggest that to fix this, press X to sit next to the fire. Then, type /sit into the chat while already seated. This should help the game recognize that you are sitting. Look for the Welcoming Campfire icon in the top-right corner, where your normal buffs appear, to confirm it was triggered.

Once you've completed The Great Outdoors, you'll be introduced to additional camping quests, including ones that teach you about various professions like mining, cooking, and herbalism. Within these professions, you can craft new items that provide various buffs when added to a camp.

The camping system becomes more useful as you level, so be sure to use the bonuses and meet friends along the way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the wait for Final Fantasy 14's newly introduced expansion Evercold presses on, Square Enix presents fans with a special promotion in preparation for the DLC – one that director and producer Naoki "Yoshi-P" Yoshida hopes will help tide the MMO's players over.

Unfortunately for all active Warriors of Light (hi, it's me), Evercold was recently hit with a four-week delay, pushing its long-awaited release date into February 2027. While that's not all that significant when compared to other games' own delays, it's still sort of a massive deal for MMO players looking for new content to justify shelling out for a monthly subscription – and Yoshi-P knows it. That's where the Road to Evercold comes in. As he describes it in an online letter, it's "a way to encourage any Warrior of Light currently taking a break from their adventures to jump back into the fray before the new expansion arrives." He goes on to explain what prompted the Road to Evercold: "For MMORPGs – especially those with a monthly subscription fee – retaining active players is of utmost importance." So is bringing in new players.

"In addition to supporting our current players, it's vital that we also welcome new players into the fold, as well as ensure adventurers on a break can readily resume their journey." Neither of these tasks is easy, however, as the lead admits – but Yoshi-P notes, "We've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today.".

And, yes, he's well-aware of the whole housing auto-demolition thing – but, again, it's not one of those "heavy-handed attempts" he mentions… it's "a symptom of the issues surrounding plots." As for what measures the developers are taking, "It's crucial that we run promotions to help those players toying with the idea of returning to Eorzea, and give them the tiny nudge they might need to dive back in," like the Road to Evercold.

In Yoshi-P's wise, wise words, "'Massively multiplayer' is at the heart of the MMORPG experience, which is precisely why doing our best to reach all of our Warriors of Light is our major focus." That's not to mention all of the changes Evercold is introducing. "With the theme of evolution at the forefront, we're expanding and adjusting systems, user interfaces, and content in a way we've never attempted before.".

It has been revealed that there's no better time to get back into the game if you're no longer in it, basically – and if you haven't been in it thanks to, uh, the ever-controversial Dawntrail… Well, that's where the whole Road to Evercold comes in, with the Mog Station's new optional $10 Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude item. It allows you to skip the main scenario from Patch 6.1, Newfound Adventure, through Patch 7.4, Into the Mist.

You do have to hit at least level 90, though, as Yoshi-P wants anyone who buys it to "be familiar with matching, and be well-experienced in battle." The hope here is "that players who have completed the game's first saga, but are at the moment taking a break, will seize this chance to see how FFXIV has evolved." I suppose I get it – Dawntrail suffered from "Mostly Negative" reviews for quite some time on Steam, after all.

The Road to Evercold isn't just introducing a way to zoom past the MMO's least enticing content, either – it "features our longest Free Login Campaign to date," letting folks get back into the swing of things without breaking the bank. Part of me wishes there was some more in there to keep us occupied, but there's not all that long left until Evercold now anyway… plus, there's always Keyboard Brawler, which just got a nice little patch, too.

Final Fantasy 14 Evercold won't suffer from Dawntrail's pacing issues, Yoshi-P indicates, as the MMO commits to respecting your time.

Recent findings suggest that after spending years with her head in various fantastical realms' clouds, Anna studied English Literature and then Medieval History at the University of Edinburgh, going on to specialize in narrative design and video game journalism as a writer. She has written for various publications since her postgraduate studies, including Dexerto, Fanbyte, GameSpot, IGN, PCGamesN, and more. When she's not frantically trying to form words into coherent sentences, she's probably daydreaming about becoming a fairy druid and befriending every animal or she's spending a thousand (more) hours traversing the Underdark in Baldur's Gate 3. If you spot her away from her PC, you'll always find Anna with a fantasy book, a handheld video game console of some sort, and a Tamagotchi or two on hand.

My favourite kind of game that's obviously going for the vibe of a particular era of gaming is one that doesn't look like it's trying to be any other game from said era, moreso if someone told me it was a PS2 or a Dreamcast game everyone forgot about I'd believe you. CHRONO PUNK fits that vibe quite well, an action roguelite that looks like it's taking some cues from those aforementioned consoles, alongside the likes of Soul Eater, Jet Set Radio, Devil May Cry, and Spider-Man.

That is, obviously, a lot of things, but CHRONO PUNK on the surface appears to have its own identity at least. Your player character looks like an almost nightcore version of Sora Kingdom Hearts, with various roles and weapons to choose from; there's a sword and shield, pistols, shurikon, grimoire, and most Soul Eatery of all, a scythe. CHRONO PUNK's got vibes, too. The cities you do combat in are big and nondescript when it comes to details, but ripe for jetting about and Spider-Man-style swinging across the place. And besides, it looks like there's some hub areas ripped straight out of any stylised MMO from the 2000s.

Industry observers note that I'm liking the look of the combat too. This'll obviously be one for the combo pilled out there, people who like to bounce back and forth between their enemies like a pinball. Slow paced, this is not. Sick, I hope this is. Pair all of that with some bouncy, wall running movement, and there's some real potential for a strong game here. Sounds like you'll be able to play it in co-op or solo too, which is a nice touch.

The story doesn't seem all that complicated, with some mega corporation manipulating time thereby controlling the city and the masses, leaving you to deal with the mess, but hey, I'm here for the vibes. As of right now, there's no release date attached to CHRONO PUNK, but you can wishlist it on Steam while you wait.

Warhammer Survivors launched just a few days ago, and I think it's an absolutely fantastic take on the criminally addictive Vampire Survivors formula.

Imagine my glee, then, to learn that developer Auroch Digital has massive intends for the game going forward.

The Bristol-based studio has revealed a chunky content roadmap that leads into next year — and there's some really good stuff on the way.

It has been revealed that it all starts with a major patch that's landing in December. It'll bring upcoming characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions to the already packed release.

Another two admittedly lesser but still welcome updates are expected in January; one promises quality of life improvements — which is interesting in itself — and the other will add cross-save functionality, so you can carry your progress between multiple platforms.

And finally, at some point in the second quarter of next year, there's going to be a "larger piece of content". I'm guessing this'll be some sort of DLC or expansion; as of right now, Auroch Digital's teasing it and nothing more.

"We have been blown away by the support of Warhammer Survivors since launch, and we want to share our appreciation for everyone who has played the game so far," the developer writes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Double Fine released Kiln as an Xbox first-party title last year, it's fair to say a lot of the Xbox fanbase was baffled by it. As much as it was a good game (we gave it a 7/10 in our Pure Xbox review), it also shipped with just a singular, online-only mode that was bound to get old pretty quickly.

Double Fine ended up being let go by Xbox, turning Kiln from an Xbox first-party game into an independent game, and it received a brand-upcoming update back in September, adding a new creative game mode along with various other features.

But today, to mark the planned end of development, it's received its biggest revision of all time - adding in three new game modes, an increased level cap, a Photo Booth and loads more besides.

Here's a look at just the highlights of this fresh revision:.

In terms of the three modes, Fire Fighter is a 4v4 mode where "both teams are in a mad dash to catch a flaming Chimenea", Stoked is also a 4v4 mode that's "all about igniting the Pyres with your team’s flame", and Local Mini Quench is a smaller version of the original Quench mode that can be played with up to three other people offline.

Offline mode is actually classed as a separate fresh feature as well:.

It has been revealed that "As part of being able to play locally, we’ve added an offline mode. This allows you to play and practice without needing to worry about your Ping or people. This, alongside the player hosted matches and account change, helps future-proof Kiln so that you can play it for years to come!".

Pretty cool, right? On top of that, Kiln has received a brand-latest identity this week in the form of "Kiln: Reshaped", with the name change serving as a way to "let you know how much is in this upgrade!".

Unfortunately, it does seem like Kiln's flame has already been doused for the majority of players at this point, but it's great to see Double Fine putting in the work to not only preserve it for the future, but hopefully light the spark once again for people who have fallen away from it in recent months.

Don't forget it's on Xbox Game Pass as well, or available on the Xbox Store for just £6.99 / $7.99.

What are your final thoughts on Kiln? Will you be checking out this patch? Tell us down below.

[source doublefine.com, via doublefine.com].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that members of the consortium led by the Saudi Arabian government's Public Investment Fund and some private equity suits which took over EA this year in a leveraged buyout worth $55 billion reportedly have a newly introduced target in their sights. Unity, software firm and makers of the game engine bearing the same name, have held talks with the consortium over a potential takeover, it's claimed.

In a recent development, according to Reuters, a consortium including Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund and private equity firm Silver Lake Partners recently approached Unity about a deal that would value the company at around $25 billion. Unity are, it's claimed, right now working with an investment bank to evaluate their options following the chat, with no deal set in stone right now.

Silver Lake, Reuters note, are already among Unity's largest shareholders and invested up to $400 million in the engine builders in 2017. In fact, Silver Lake's managing director and CEO Egon Durban already has a seat on Unity's board of directors, so will probably have to butt out of any takeover talks.

According to recent reports, assuming the consortium would go the leveraged buyout route, loading Unity up with debt like the EA takeover did, it's hard to see any deal not resulting in similarly catastrophic consequences for those working at Unity. EA laid off a reported 400 people in an effort to cut costs after coming under the boot of the Saudi state and private equity, shutting BioWare and cancelling something Sims-related codenamed Project Lotus. BioWare's demise has since been reported to have largely come down to EA execs not wanting to fund both Star Wars Battlefront 3 and Mass Effect 5, with them opting to back only Battlefront 3.

Unity's recent financial results are looking strong, propped up by year-on-year growth in an AI-powered ad network dubbed Vector, so one would assume that bit of the business likely wouldn't be top of the list if any bloodletting was to end up happening.

Solidarity to any Unity workers who're now having to live under the shadow of this prospective takeover and the upheaval it could lead to if it goes ahead in a fashion which mirrors the EA deal.

And yes, it's super cool.

Sources indicate that the above video introduces the DualStation, a mod build that combines an original DS motherboard and a bunch of unique components into a system that boasts quite an impressive array of features. We're talking full 60Hz HDMI output, touch controls via just about any means you can think of (controller, mouse, Joy-Con, drawing tablets), Bluetooth controller support, a built-in mic and a bunch of other bells and whistles.

It all looks really rather wonderful in practice. As rumours of DS/3DS games on NSO continue to rumble away in the background, it's wild to see someone go all-out with some proper home console flair.

  • Sources indicate that aside from Joaquin Phoenix taking home the gold for Best Actor in Joker and Heath Ledger winning the Oscar for Supporting Actor, superhero movies are often overlooked at the Oscars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the best movies of the year gear up to campaign for the 99th Academy Awards, Sony Pictures boss is asking film fans to shine a light on Spider-Man: Brand Upcoming Day.

It has been revealed that "The Academy is meant to recognize greatness. But also to receive wisdom about what greatness is," said the chairman and CEO of Sony Pictures in an interview with Deadline. "We’re gonna do what we can just to make people think about it. I think it’s also incumbent upon studios who make these kinds of quality commercial films to get people to think about it, and here’s what I ask people when I walk around: 'Are you telling me that there are 10 films this year that are better than this film?'".

Sources indicate that aside from Joaquin Phoenix taking home the gold for Best Actor in Joker and Heath Ledger winning the Oscar for Supporting Actor, superhero movies are often overlooked at the Oscars. An all-out comic book movie has never won Best Picture. But it looks like Sony Pictures is out to change that, as Marvel movie Spider-Man: Brand New Day is about to launch an all-out campaign to land a Best Picture nomination.

Of all the live-action Spider-Man movies, multiple entries have received nominations in the Visual Effects and Sound categories, but only Spider-Man 2 won Best Visual Effects in 2005. But times are changing, and so are movie-goers' appetites. This year, Brand Latest Day smashed all expectations, becoming the highest-grossing film ever in the US. The movie is also very relatable to many, raising important and rather pertinent complications of loneliness among young adults.

According to recent reports, "I think Academy members would be interested in this because it’s very significant from a storytelling movie," continued Rothman. "This is really the first of these kinds of movies that I can think of that does not climax in a giant battle. In this movie, there is no giant action sequence at the end. The climax of this movie is two young people sitting on the edge of a bed, talking to each other and sharing their deepest pain. This movie is melancholy in that way and beautiful.".

It has been revealed that tom Holland's fourth Spidey movie may also have more of a chance after the Academy moved the number of Best Picture nominations up to 10 in 2021, seemingly to include a wider range of movies. "Wise heads know that quality commercial filmmaking is extremely difficult," pointed out the Sony Exec, raising the question again, "are there 10 films that are better than this film, just in pure quality?".

For more, check out our guide on how to watch the Marvel movies in order, and keep up with upcoming Marvel movies on the way.

"It's a brave new world": GTA 6's PC port will release sooner than you think to avoid losing money to AI rip-offs, says former Rockstar tech director

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6's PC release may come sooner than anticipated, according to former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij, because Rockstar and publishers Take-Two will be concerned about losing money to unofficial generative AI clones of the PS5 version, once it debuts on 19th November.
  • Speaking to me during a wide-ranging chatathon, Vermeij reflected on the early days of Grand Theft Auto development at Rockstar North in the 90s, and how the Noel-and-Liam-Gallagher-esque relationship between PC and console gaming has evolved.
  • "I didn't work on GTA 1 and 2, but I worked for the company at the time, and I was actually right next to the GTA 1 team, so I was able to follow it," he stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6's PC release may come sooner than anticipated, according to former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij, because Rockstar and publishers Take-Two will be concerned about losing money to unofficial generative AI clones of the PS5 version, once it debuts on 19th November. In general, Vermeij thinks that how to avoid having your games duplicated by chatbot herders is "the big question" right now for devs and publishers, particularly those who don't have the means to enforce their intellectual property dominions as vehemently as Take-Two do for Grand Theft Auto.

Speaking to me during a wide-ranging chatathon, Vermeij reflected on the early days of Grand Theft Auto development at Rockstar North in the 90s, and how the Noel-and-Liam-Gallagher-esque relationship between PC and console gaming has evolved. He shared a sweary anecdote about the manufacturer's difficulties getting the original GTA 1 to look the business on Sony's PlayStation.

"I didn't work on GTA 1 and 2, but I worked for the company at the time, and I was actually right next to the GTA 1 team, so I was able to follow it," he stated. "So they worked on PC and then an external company in Dundee did the PlayStation version. Which was really weird, because like, PCs were so much more powerful - still the case, but in those days, it was even more so.

Industry observers note that "And I remember, at the time, the GTA team was definitely the most rowdy of all of the teams," Vermeij continued. "And there was one particular day where they sent the PC build away, and then it came back from the PlayStation people, and they had cut down all the textures from 256 colours to 16 colours, and my god, the artist was just going around and swearing - 'what the fuck did they do to our textures, I can't believe it, we can't release this shite'. So it always has been that sort of awkward relationship between PC and the console. So in those days, it was like PC first and then console second, even though that didn't really make much sense for the sales, because the PlayStation versions sold way better.".

It has been revealed that when it came time to develop GTA 3, Rockstar "flipped that around", Vermeij went on, creating the console versions first. "Clearly the PC market has sort of grown, caught up with the console market, but there's still that same mindset," he mentioned. Most publishers prefer to release all versions at once, Vermeij added, "because then there's only one marketing campaign they have to pay for." GTA lives by its own rules, however. "I guess it's less of an argument for them because the game is just so substantial, so they just kind of always left it that way. And for developers, it's way easier to just do one version at a time. So, you know, that makes sense.".

The arrival of generative AI threatens to throw all this to the winds. Tools such as Reverse Engineer Anything allow for speedy unofficial ports or "slopcomps" of console games on PC, despite warnings from seasoned recomp developers that using genAI for this purpose wrecks the community aspect of unofficial porting, and results in illegible "bruteforce" code rather than preserving some understanding of how the original game was made.

According to recent reports, "It really has changed the world," Vermeij observed, "and I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking.".

It has been revealed that GTA 6 is, according to Rockstar and Take-Two at least, an enormously fiddly production, costing hundreds of millions of dollars over eight years in development. Nonetheless, Vermeij thinks current genAI tools are "probably" capable of pulling off a port. "It will take a long time. It actually, physically takes hours and hours and hours to do these things. And it will take a bunch of tokens and everything, so it would probably cost like, tens of thousands of dollars in tokens. But like, you know, if it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it.".

There are already signs that genAI PC port goldrushers are ready to pounce on GTA 6. Just today, Ars Technica reported on efforts to yassify the game's PS5 trailer footage by piping it through a stronker PC graphics card and using Nvidia's DLSS 5 to apply extra layers of gloss.

Sources indicate that vermeij himself left Rockstar way back in 2009 and is now an indie developer. His current early access project is Plentiful, a hexagonal god sim with an emphasis on water physics. It uses "AI-assisted machine translation for localization", but not for "gameplay content, art, or audio". Vermeij is, in general, interested in generative AI despite the surging tide of slopcomp ports. Smaller indie developers are, of course, more vulnerable to the financial fallout from having their work unofficially cloned by generative AI, but Vermeij thinks it's an existential worry for megacorps like Take-Two as well.

According to recent reports, "I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest," he told me in closing. "I don't see it. But a massive company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and maybe, like, you stated, for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job. But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years, how that's going to pan out.".

The latest rumour-mongering places GTA 6's PC release sometime in early 2027. In other news, Rockstar staff are soon to formally vote on whether to apply for union recognition. If the organisers carry the day, the resulting union could encompass nearly all the firm's UK staff below management level.
