💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially debuted, nearly six years after it was initially revealed.
  • All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.
  • It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert rolled out on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially debuted, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert rolled out on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

Sources indicate that the action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it rolled out. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

Sources indicate that this peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”.

If you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or blueprint to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

If you don't feel berated enough in Ocarina of Time, you can now add a full-size fairy to watch judgmentally from the shelf because a fan just made their own version of Lego Navi.

According to recent reports, the finished product was posted over at Reddit by AdatheB, and it's instantly recognizable as Link's fairy companion. Presumably made using spare parts of a kind you'd find on Lego's Pick a Brick store page, their Lego Navi figure is around six to seven inches tall and 'floats' on a clear stand. It's also the closest we're likely to get to a full-size kit, because as of right now the only official model is a tiny stud Navi in the Ocarina of Time Final Battle set (available at Amazon) and the now-retired Deku Tree, AKA one of the best Lego sets.

As the post's top comment from CommunicationSea3329 notes, "Lego should listen to your idea.".

This isn't the first time AdatheB has created their own gaming-themed Lego set; in a reply on the same Reddit thread, they show off their full shelves where Navi now lives, and it features figures like a Hollow Knight kit and multiple Lego Pikmin. With that in mind, I think the above comment is right, and Nintendo should start following AdatheB's example. I'd love to have a Pikmin set perched above my Switch, for instance.

In the here and now, this fan-made kit stands out because, generally speaking, there's not much actual Navi merch. The best you can usually expect is third-party gear like keychains (such as this unnamed-but-clearly-Navi one at Amazon) or earrings. However, with the popularity of the Ocarina of Time remake, I wouldn't be surprised to see more in the not-so-distant future.

  • Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.
  • In the first case, at least, something is being done.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental complications that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”.

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest upgrade only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

Recent findings suggest that the most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer mentioned we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

It has been revealed that if you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added latest pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, I do not wish to "rule the streets" of Megacity West, dear creators of Airframe Ultra.
  • Sources indicate that those eroded pastel chevrons.
  • Despite my best efforts, Airframe Ultra is a battle racer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I do not wish to "rule the streets" of Megacity West, dear creators of Airframe Ultra. I wish to be ravished by them, rubbing my face against the rusty corrugated metal of the shipping containers, and savouring the acid blue waters of the bay. I do not want to "become the one thing with freedom in a city of billions: A racer." I want to become the other thing with freedom in a city of billions: a person who slowly drives or – whisper it - walks around just looking at stuff, because gadzooks, this is one of the prettiest PS1 cyberpunk burgs I've laid eyes on.

Sources indicate that those eroded pastel chevrons. Those seductively wobbling vertices. That electric reef of a downtown backdrop, murderously luring your gaze from the on-coming trucks. That layer of invigorating crackle over everything. Every moment or so, I dismount from my hoverbike to inspect some concrete ruin I could swear I last saw in G-Police, or ponder the resemblance between a subway tunnel and WipEout 2097's Gare d'Europa. Then, somebody waps me in the skull with a stop sign at 300 kilometres an hour. But I was already stopped, frantic stranger! Your brutal poetic ironies are wasted on me.

Despite my best efforts, Airframe Ultra is a battle racer. It's co-developed by Videocult, the people behind Rain World – a game it looks nothing like, but is comparable to in the sense that there is an ocean of industrial refuse to navigate, and you will very often die. Each battle race is broken into sprints around a branching course that has been smashed together by the forces of urban decay. You will corkscrew down storm drains and barge through old abandoned clifftop mansions under a scarlet sun, zip along deadly flyovers and thread the barely legible layouts of high density slums.

Your hoverbike handles like a bronco full of helium, and that's before you start wanging it off the gloriously marbled, low-poly rubbish heaps that stud the city, shunting the game's camera through surfaces and exposing the map's underside in what the absolute squares amongst my readers will doubtless deem "an inelegance", but which true turbojunkeys will appreciate for its makeshift exuberance.

You've got a boost button which generally gets you exploded – and all that's before you get to the time-limited battle arenas that bookend each sprint. Here, players attempt to slaughter each other as much as possible, spending collectible cash on floating weapon pick-ups that range from bent pipes to Gatling guns and EMP grenades. Then it's off for another sprint. The first player to earn 10 points and place first in a subsequent sprint wins the match. I have not won many matches. My primary goal right now in Airframe Ultra is persuading everybody to stop and swap some emotes, while I coo over an amazing piece of graffiti I've found.

My efforts to make Airframe Ultra a walking sim aren't just about scenery. The game is surprisingly engrossing on foot, with some woozy tank controls that make me think of the experimental days before every third-person control scheme became a variation on Assassin's Creed, Uncharted or Gears of War. You have to hammer a button to run, for instance, and you'll wind yourself fast. You can also perform punches and kicks in four directions, with grander attacks to discover by smooshing together inputs. You'd best believe I burst into tears when I realised what this reminded me of: it's Bungie's Oni! The game with the finest martial arts system ever coded! There are more obvious influences, like Road Rash, but in these grim days of endless parrying, I'll take all the Konoko callbacks I can get.

Ahhhhh. But if only this had a proper single player mode. Online and local splitscreen with drop-in bot support are all you get. I wouldn't say Airframe is the most balanced deathracer, either. In my experience, and do bear in mind I mostly try to avoid the racing component, victory typically goes to whoever lands a fat cash reserve and grabs an AK47. That mild shambolicness is arguably part of the charm, in that it supplies incentive to stop and drink in the atmosphere. These streets are massive and broken and beautiful enough for all of us, friends. Let us rule them together. Read more on Steam.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that scouting in Football Manager 27 hasn't seen any major overhauls, but the system is still much deeper today than it was even in FM 24, and can be overwhelming for beginners.
  • We'll take you through some key aspects of scouting and why it's just as important as upcoming features like Tactical Effectiveness for a successful career in FM 27.
  • The first thing you should do when you start a new save, regarding scouting, is to check your scouting budget and make sure your scouting range is appropriate for the type of scouting you'll be doing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that scouting in Football Manager 27 hasn't seen any major overhauls, but the system is still much deeper today than it was even in FM 24, and can be overwhelming for beginners. If you're the kind of player who typically lets their staff identify players to sign but occasionally likes to scout the odd South American wonderkid, this guide is for you.

We'll take you through some key aspects of scouting and why it's just as important as upcoming features like Tactical Effectiveness for a successful career in FM 27.

The first thing you should do when you start a new save, regarding scouting, is to check your scouting budget and make sure your scouting range is appropriate for the type of scouting you'll be doing.

At top-flight clubs, this will be set to "World" by default, and that's fine, but in saves outside the top leagues, or in countries where the money doesn't flow quite so much, you may have to make adjustments to get the most out of your scouting budget.

Remember, you can assign some of your transfer budget to your scouting budget if you need to upgrade your scouting range.

Your scouting range refers to the area your scouts will search for players whenever you send them on recruitment focuses or when they are generally looking for talent when directed by the chief scout. There is still a scout associated with specific player scouting that comes out of your total budget, and you can still scout players outside of your base scouting range for a cost, but you won't naturally get worldwide scouting results if your scouting range is set to the local area or a specific continent.

To have the best chance of finding the players with the most potential, or just having scouting reports with accurate player data, you need to ensure your scouts are up to the task.

The three stats that matter most to scouts are Judging Player Ability, Judging Player Potential, and Adaptability. The first two are self-explanatory: they determine how well a scout can assess a player's current ability and stats, and their potential. Adaptability, however, relates to how quickly a scout can set up for their next task and how efficiently they feed back the data. Scouts with better adaptability can scout unfamiliar territories more efficiently and take less time to start feeding back results.

A final point to consider for your scouts is their knowledge base. You can find this on their profile, and it demonstrates which countries they know best. Scouts can have multiple strong knowledge bases, and you want as much diversity as possible on your team to make scouting around the world more fruitful.

Industry observers note that glossing over player reports is a sin, because you're bound to miss notable information that could turn what looks like a world-class signing into a dud. When reading a scout report, the first thing to pay attention to is the report's level of knowledge. Anything less than extensive could lead to assumptions, misjudging the severity of certain traits, or missing them entirely. Your scout also won't be able to narrow down a player's attributes until their knowledge of the player is complete. This means selecting the option to "Fully Scout" a player if you're targeting someone not already in your scouting recommendations.

When reading the report, pay close attention to the wording, especially in the cons. This is where you'll find out whether a player is injury-prone, has a poor personality, is inconsistent, will demand high agent fees, and has a range of other negative traits.

It has been revealed that finally, when rating the player against others on your team, ensure your scout is comparing them for the right position. Players who can play multiple positions are typically rated against the position they are most proficient in, but if you're bringing them in to play somewhere else, you can have the scouting report rate them against your existing options there instead.

Recent findings suggest that the final tip for scouting in FM 27 is to use both the Squad Planner and Comparison tools. Squad Planner lets you see the depth in your current team; it's a great starting point for building your squad and understanding exactly who your starters are and where your depth lies.

Recent findings suggest that you can also add scouted targets to the Squad Planner to see how strong your positional ratings would be if you make certain signings. While the Squad Planner has been in FM for a number of years, so many players still don't use it, yet it's such a helpful tool, especially for influencing your scouting for the season.

The Comparison tool, on the other hand, is a very common tool, but it's still worth us flagging that it exists and is a great way to directly compare two players. In this case, we'd be comparing incoming signings to existing players. When a player is fully scouted, you can compare their attributes directly with players on your team to see who comes out on top. Obviously, intangibles like personality still need to be considered, but this is a great base to build on when you're scouting to directly replace a specific player.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, fresh reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

Industry observers note that the rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance Upcoming Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

Recent findings suggest that however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance Newly introduced Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Industry observers note that kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

In a recent development, marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no confirmed platforms.

Recent findings suggest that although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

[Sources: Jason Schreier, Kotaku].

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that as part of the console brand's 25th anniversary, Microsoft has released a magazine about Xbox's past, present, and future.
  • Industry observers note that obviously, the biggest conversations about the Xbox Project Helix – and the PS6 – are cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A lead developer on Xbox Project Helix states that rising hardware costs are a primary driver of the upcoming console's development.

It has been revealed that as part of the console brand's 25th anniversary, Microsoft has released a magazine about Xbox's past, present, and future. This online magazine includes an interview with Jason Ronald, vice president of next-generation console development at Microsoft and the lead for Project Helix. In this interview, he clarifies that Xbox Project Helix is "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," rather than the other way around.

Industry observers note that obviously, the biggest conversations about the Xbox Project Helix – and the PS6 – are cost. Hardware prices are rising thanks to the ongoing global RAM shortages brought on by AI companies who just need to let your weird uncle generate what he looks like as a Simpson to post on Facebook. The Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and Nintendo Switch 2 have all had price increases over the past year, but Ronald claims keeping the price down is a crucial motivator in the console's design.

"It's definitely a challenging time," Ronald indicates, adding, "it’s also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely fresh technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable.".

He explains the cost factor is why the team behind Project Helix is "really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it’s an entirely upcoming way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that.".

Obviously AI-assisted tech was a massive talking point within games before the memory crisis, but it feels like it's only going to become more prominent. Sony has been implementing QSSR frame generation tech into its PS5 games, likely in part because nobody can afford a PS5 Pro now that it's almost $1,000.

And with things going like they are, it's probably going to be the norm heading forward… let's just hope Xbox puts its money where its mouth is and actually makes the Helix affordable. But given the current rumor is it's going to be $1,800, I'm not too hopeful.

If PS6 and Xbox Project Helix are $1,000, 5-year sales could drop by 40%, analyst notes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I may be very late to the party with this discovery, but I only just realised you can connect your Steam Wishlist to a third-party deals tracker. The beauty of which is that, once hooked up, you can see what games you've been pining for are going cheap not just on Steam but through any major shopfront across the internet.

I worry that I will be coming across as 'Use this one trick to save money – greengrocers hate it!', but it's already helped save my nephew more than £40. Even if it meant using a slightly underhand method.

Two weeks ago, I got a text from my nephew asking what the best way to play Total War: Warhammer 3. When I messaged back a couple of hours later (look, I'm not a responsive uncle) to tell him it's presently £50 on Steam, but it's worth waiting because according to SteamDB's price history it's come down to £7.50 in the past, I was too late. He'd got itchy feet and bought it at full whack on Steam, using up all his birthday money.

That's when I went looking and found Is There Any Deal for the first time. (A lot of you in the comments may be throwing your hands up in despair to hear this oversight) If you've not come across it before, it's a site that tracks game sales across loads of shops, including Steam, EA Store, Epic Games Store, GamersGate, GOG. GreenManGaming, Humble. This means while a game may not be on sale on Steam you can see if it's on sale anywhere else.

In the case of Total War: Warhammer 3, while it was full price on Steam, over on the Humble Store it was discounted to £7.49. I sent a link to my nephew and then told him, using the authority only an uncle has, that it's okay to refund the game through Steam and buy the cheaper version. It's not something I've ever done myself, but he's 17 and that is a lot of money to save.

Sources indicate that anyway, that's recommendation the first. It was only when I was looking for a way to export my Steam Wishlist to ask RPS supporters what I should cull that I realised Is There Any Deal has another feature: you can import every game on your Wishlist to get deal notifications. (This may get a second groan of despair in the comment section.) Once linked up, the site will ping you a notification whenever games you're waiting for pop up in a deal.

Sources indicate that just looking at my current list, I can get Genesis Noir, Ancient Enemy, and Norco for £10 total, all of which with more than 70% discounts through stores other than Steam. So, as you can see, this could be both a saving technically and lead me to spending a lot more money than I mean to….

You may already have heard of these tools, but as I hadn't I thought it best to give them a shout out.

Now considering I've revealed myself to be a rube, what other third party tools should I be installing to weaponise my Steam Library?

In a recent development, age of Empires-influenced real-time strategy game The Fertile Crescent 2: Collapse of the Bronze Age leaves early access today, publishers MicroProse have announced, with the 1.0 version adding the final chapters of the singleplayer story. You'll also get your grubby fingers on the very same map editor developers Wield Interactive used to design the campaign.

I'm new to The Fertile Crescent 2 myself. I do like the sound of a strategy sim in which you guide a fugitive community through the Late Bronze Age Collapse. The land has been thrown into turmoil by the arrival of the Sea People, this being a loose historical term for assorted ocean-going migrants who, I gather, are often blamed for the crumbling of the Hittites among other once-glorious Bronze Age powers. I don't have much scholarly insight to share - I thought the "Sea People" referred to expansionist mermaids, at first - but I do have a trailer.

Nate Crowley (RPS in peace) was exceedingly fond of the original game, calling it "a bite-sized chunk of phenomenal RTS design" that "manages to riff nostalgically on Age Of Empires, while completely rewriting its ground rules". The sequel continues with the same core concepts – above all, the paramount importance of food, which determines population and army size together with your civ's progression.

"This is not a game about building the biggest empire," the developers explain in a press release. "Resources have to be managed, stability is fragile, and growth comes with risk. Every expansion, every battle, and every decision must be weighed against survival. Building and managing a sustainable economy is as crucial as commanding your forces in battle. Expanding your army too rapidly can put your food economy under pressure.".

Sources indicate that the story spans 17 missions, with four playable factions: the Assyrians, Egyptians, Babylonians, and Hittites. The 1.0 release also includes some standalone scenario missions, a skirmish mode, and multiplayer on dedicated servers with bot support.

In a recent development, read more on Steam. If you're partial to historical strategy and don't mind winding back the clock (upturning the hourglass? Adjusting the sundial? Recalibrating the henge?) another few thousand years, Folk Emerging is pretty terrific. If you like stories about migrant tribes, and you don't mind trading your Hittites for Vikings, you might get a kick out of The Banner Saga.

Industry observers note that today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some substantial news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a massive expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

It has been revealed that as part of this new enhancement, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a fresh boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only upcoming character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her major gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Recent findings suggest that linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Sources indicate that beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

It has been revealed that this update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no newly introduced characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

Despite being ousted from DC Studios in the wake of Skydance Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros., James Gunn has still found time to debunk rumors about the status of upcoming Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow.

Writing on Threads – where else? – Gunn stated, "There are a lot of untrue rumors going around, but one of them is that Skydance has seen Man of Tomorrow and that all sorts of sweeping changes are being made.".

The ex-DC Studios co-CEO added, "No one from Skydance has even seen the movie – the only people that have are [fellow ex-co-CEO] Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false.".

Whispers had circulated that Skydance would be getting more hands-on with Man of Tomorrow as its fresh DCU vision began to take shape.

According to recent reports, in early November, Gunn and Safran stepped down as heads of DC Studios, with one-time Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham taking over from December 1. In a statement, Gunn admitted he was "incredibly relieved to get back to pure filmmaking" but little is known at this current juncture about what will happen with the overall vision put forth by Gunn as part of DCU Chapter One: Gods and Monsters.

Sources indicate that man of Tomorrow, meanwhile, features a who's who of the DCU, including David Corenswet, Nicholas Hoult, Rachel Brosnahan, Edi Gathegi, Nathan Fillion, Milly Alcock, Aaron Pierre, and Xolo Mariduena. Matthew Lillard is also in the cast, with the actor confirming he will play an original character not found in the comic books.

Man of Tomorrow hits cinemas on July 9, 2027. For more, we have a guide to upcoming superhero movies.

  • This Pokémon Pokopia guide explains how to start the Apples to Applin event, how to get Syrupy Apples, and everything you need to find Applin evolutions Flapple, Appleun, Dipplin and Hydrapple.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Apples to Applin event runs from 16th November to 1st December, 2026, adding five Gen 8 Pokémon to Pokémon Pokopia.

If you've played previous limited-time events, you'll know what to expect. A upcoming Pokémon, Applin, will drop outside the Pokémon Center, asking you to find a currency (Syrupy Apples) in exchange for new items, helping you construct several brand new habitats.

This Pokémon Pokopia guide explains how to start the Apples to Applin event, how to get Syrupy Apples, and everything you need to find Applin evolutions Flapple, Appleun, Dipplin and Hydrapple.

Before you start, you need to have rebuilt a Pokémon Center. Once done, make sure you have the latest update, and are playing between the dates of 16th November to 1st December, 2026.

Sources indicate that as with recent live-events in the second half of the year, you couldn't time travel to this event ahead of time. But once the start date has passed and once you've connected the game to the internet to authenticate the date, you are able to time travel back if you missed it.

To get Syrupy Apples, you must visit Dream Islands with the help of Drifloon by interacting with a doll.

Once in a Dream Island, look for apples growing on trees; give them a headbutt and collect your spoils.

You'll find around 40-50 per visit, meaning you'll need to visit on another day to get 80, which is enough to buy one of every event item (or if you're simply unlocking the event habitats, then you just need 70).

Alternatively, can grow your own Syrupy Apple Tree by buying Syrupy Apple Seeds during the event - one of which is a requirement for one of the habitats - if you so choose, allowing you to source Syrupy Apples in a location of your choosing.

When you have some Syrupy Apples, you can head to the Pokémon Center and exchange them at the counter for event-specific items. These are:.

The Apples to Applin event has three habitats to unlock:.

This means you need to acquire a total of 70 Syrupy Apples to get items for three Habitats.

Unlike past events, this isn't a simple case of buying and combining the items, as the Abundant Apples and Apple Kitchen requires some additional prep and / or other items first.

For Abundant Apples's Syrupy Apple Tree, plant a Syrupy Apple Seed tree in soil prepared with the Rototiller, then water it each day until it grows and sprouts fruit, turning it into a Syrupy Apple Tree.

This will take around three to four days in total, though you can always change the time to do this quicker, and is definitely not what we did to speed up the process.

As for Apple Kitchen's Kitchen Table, if you don't have one already, you can find one of these in the building on the edge of the water west of the Pokémon Center in Bleak Beach (see the mini-map in the below screenshot for the exact location). From there, you can use a 3D Printer to copy a couple more.

Best of luck getting all three habitats before the event wraps!

This isn't the first Pokémon Pokopia event we've covered. And if meeting Applin and their many evolutions has inspired you to keep playing, our Pokémon Pokopia walkthrough leads the way to many more guides that can help.

Ubisoft has just greenlit and entered the early stages of development on a third Rainbow Six: Vegas game, according to a new Insider Gaming report.

The outlet, which seems to have been clued up on internal Ubisoft happenings for years, claims the new entry is one of three projects that have just started production at Ubisoft Montreal, and one of the other two is also set in the Rainbow Six universe.

That's according to sources speaking under anonymity to the website.

According to recent reports, while the Rainbow Six name is still used to this day, most notably in Rainbow Six: Siege, the Vegas sub-series stopped in 2008, after the release of Rainbow Six: Vegas 2. This reported third instalment enters development 18 years later.

Recent findings suggest that sources discussing the matter with Insider Gaming suggest the project is most likely Vegas 3, and not a remake of the previous entries. It's apparently very early in development, though, so don't expect a public reveal for a number of years — that is if it doesn't get cancelled before then.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that early last month, Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor brought back a number of developers who had been furloughed before the game rolled out in August.
  • It has been revealed that as spotted by Star Wars outlet Bespin Bulletin, multiple developers shared word of their layoffs to LinkedIn.
  • Tyler Eichten, a UI engineer, also mentioned, "As of today, my time with Bit Reactor has come to a close due to a layoff.

Industry observers note that early last month, Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor brought back a number of developers who had been furloughed before the game rolled out in August. At the time they did not specify how many devs were returning to the studio, with a separate report claiming more than half had become full time staffers again. Unfortunately, it does now seem like not everyone was able to be brought back, with a number of now former workers sharing word of having been laid off.

It has been revealed that as spotted by Star Wars outlet Bespin Bulletin, multiple developers shared word of their layoffs to LinkedIn. A producer at Bit Reactor, Michael Blackard was seemingly one of the first to report being laid off, alongside senior QA analyst Ryan Mosher. Ryan Lopez, an environment artist at the studio, shared, "I was laid off from Bit Reactor this week after a three-month furlough, and while it stings, I’m really proud of what we built together." Lopez had apparently been working on the game for more than three years, starting all the way back on the game's pre-production period.

Tyler Eichten, a UI engineer, also mentioned, "As of today, my time with Bit Reactor has come to a close due to a layoff. I am immensely proud of the work that I, the UI/UX team, and the team at large have accomplished. I hope that in this tumultuous industry that my coworkers (and myself) find placement." It's unclear at this point in time if any, or how many, other staffers have been formally laid off, and Bit Reactor are yet to make a comment.

Star Wars Zero Company performed very well both critically and commercially, making it all the more disappointing that not all of those who worked on the game, who made it as great as it seemingly is, get to continue working at the studio. As always, solidarity with all devs affected.

After James Gunn was surprisingly ousted from DC, Star-Lord actor Chris Pratt is open to the director returning to Marvel.

Gunn was previously co-CEO of DC Studios, but news broke recently that he and his co-CEO Peter Safran were out following the Paramount and Warner Bros. merger to create Skydance.

"That would be awesome," Pratt told Moviezine of the possibility of Gunn returning to Marvel. "I love working with James. He's the man. I haven't had the chance to speak with him since that news came out… it's always tough because anytime something like this comes up it could always become a headline.".

Gunn has also recently debunked rumors that Skydance has seen the upcoming Man of Tomorrow and wants changes.

"There are a lot of untrue rumors going around, but one of them is that Skydance has seen Man of Tomorrow and that all sorts of sweeping changes are being made," Gunn wrote on Threads. "No one from Skydance has even seen the movie – the only people that have are Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false.".

Man of Tomorrow arrives on July 9, 2027, and, while it's a follow-up to 2025's Superman, it's not strictly a sequel.

"I feel that sense of responsibility more acutely": After BioWare's closure, the makers of a fresh Mass Effect 3 co-op remaster mod look to carry their legacy

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (962 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It appears I was premature in suggesting that the closure of BioWare might quickly spell an end for Mass Effect 3's strangely good, preposterously enduring co-op mode.
  • This oversight has now been addressed, with the release of the Legendary Edition Multiplayer mod for mentioned remaster.
  • In a recent development, at least some of that affection can be seen in how Legendary Edition Multiplayer differs from the already-available LEMP mod, which uses AI vibecoding to slap a mechanically identical recreation of ME3's co-op into the Legendary Edition's ones and zeroes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It appears I was premature in suggesting that the closure of BioWare might quickly spell an end for Mass Effect 3's strangely good, preposterously enduring co-op mode. I reinstalled and logged on just last week, and easily found a series of packed lobbies. Still, it was always regrettable that 2021's Mass Effect Legendary Edition opted not to remaster this multiplayer component alongside its dolled-up main trilogy, thus failing to introduce to a new generation the joys of performing teleporting psychic headbutts as a millennia-old bipedal frog.

This oversight has now been addressed, with the release of the Legendary Edition Multiplayer mod for mentioned remaster. It's both a reconstruction and a slight expansion of ME3 multi, built in secret since 2023 by the ME3Tweaks group: a modding collective who've previously imbued the Legendary Edition with Mass Effect 1's Pinnacle Station DLC. It's also, some of its makers tell me, a bittersweet expression of appreciation for a series that looks unlikely to continue after EA's Mass Effect 5 cancellation.

In a recent development, at least some of that affection can be seen in how Legendary Edition Multiplayer differs from the already-available LEMP mod, which uses AI vibecoding to slap a mechanically identical recreation of ME3's co-op into the Legendary Edition's ones and zeroes. ME3Tweaks's version instead adds, according to member and longtime ME modder Audemus, a "completely overhauled UI, rebaked level lighting, upscaled and redrawn textures, upgraded shaders, native LE features such as HDR and controller support, networking and server replication improvements, extensive bug fixes, and entirely new wave modes such as Unified and Coalition.".

Unified mode, for instance, quite literally mixes up ME3's enemy factions by forming mishmashed waves of baddies from across the Geth, Reaper, and Cerberus armies, thereby dusting off and stamping on your 14-year-old battle tactics. The mod also offers the ability to use ME3Tweaks' own servers for matchmaking, though a private server option remains for scraps with mates.

I'll definitely be giving this a try, once I'm back from my current travels. Though as with those OG ME3 multiplayer sessions last week, it'll be with a certain glumness, knowing that – despite a vocal campaign to give Mass Effect 5 a reprieve– I'll be playing something that had its future cut short.

The circumstances aren't lost on Legendary Edition Multiplayer's creators. "BioWare's closure is an incredibly sad moment for the games industry, and a particularly heartbreaking thing for the Mass Effect fanbase to contend with," Audemus tells me over email. "I feel as though our responsibility as a modding community has always been to carry the torch for this franchise, with or without an official future for it. But now that the future of Mass Effect has never been more in question, I feel that sense of responsibility more acutely than I ever have before.".

Mgamerz, another modder on the project, recalls how "The day BioWare closed it didn't hit me until later in the day, a sort of numbness I can't really describe. I've spent 14 years working on their games - it's like watching a friend lose a parent - maybe you're not attached, but you feel the secondhand distress.".

For some Legendary Edition Multiplayer modders, the affected BioWare staff included developers they knew personally. ME3Tweaks had previously been invited to embargoed discussions with both BioWare and EA on game modding, and Mass Effect writer and director Mac Walters (who left BioWare voluntarily in 2023) allegedly advocated for an even closer relationship.

Recent findings suggest that "It's a shame to see it shut down," Mgamerz says. "Everyone speculated about it, but I know from talking to people internally there, that nobody knew the guillotine was about to drop." [Owners EA say the decision was only made after "months of planning, review, and analysis", though independent reporting suggests it was largely down to a straight choice between making ME5 or Star Wars Battlefront 3.].

Recent findings suggest that "When we had our NDA with BioWare (since expired), apparently Mac Walters pushed internally to get my dev team brought into the manifold," he adds. "I say this as 'apparently', cause due to scheduling issues we never got to speak with Mac. But secondhand stories tell me he was a major proponent of modders - something that I would have loved to see more publicly shown.

"It is disappointing to know that the people who helped build the world my work now builds upon were killed unceremoniously - a problem that plagues the industry, and what kept me from further pursuing entry into it, something I used to dream of doing when I was younger.".

It has been revealed that RPS lawyers are telling me to tell you that nobody was literally killed. All the same, and even as someone much more familiar with playing the Mass Effects than tinkering around in their engine bays, the ME3Tweaks team make relatable points: we can frolick around an uprezzed Firebase Hydro, biotically biffing half-robot Turians like it's 2012, but it'll be hard not to look at all those conspicuous waist-high walls and think about the people who put them there. The same's true of having your mind drift to thoughts of their successors.

But there's another way of looking at it, which is that mods like Legendary Edition Multiplayer can preserve and maintain an original developer's work well beyond what their leveraged-buyout executive overlords might deem financially inconvenient. "I hope," as Audemus puts it, "that this mod - along with the fact that we've been able to build the technology to make mods like this in the first place - sends a message that there is incredible value in this franchise, and a passionate fanbase that is not ready to say goodbye to this universe and these games.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that world of Warcraft: Forever came out last night. Those who stayed up were prepared for the usual from major WoW releases: long queues, disconnects, and server lag. However, save for a few minor hiccups here and there, things went off without a hitch.

Eurogamer can report first-hand that for European players who stayed up from, let's say 11pm - 3:50am last night, the login queues were short and constantly moving. Those who were very keen to get in the moment servers went live ran into unclickable server selection boxes, but backing out and re-joining the short queue fixed this problem swiftly.

According to recent reports, once you got in, there was very little server lag save for a lost spell cast or two, nor were constant random disconnects that would boot you out into the cold (I didn't get disconnected once - a record). As far as WoW launches go, an incredibly smooth first day.

This was acknowledged by World of Warcraft developers, such as executive producer Holly Longdale who wrote on X: "At the risk of jinxing things, so far so goodish which is crazy by itself. The team prepared a lot since the wildness of Beta. And this launch was crazier than the insanity we imagined but thankfully the team built aims and contingencies. They are incredible in my opinion.".

Josh "Aggrend" Greenfield, a senior game designer on World of Warcraft Forever, addressed some minor issues that did pop up. These include a zone population problem: in basic terms the megaservers split players into different shards, and some of these felt a bit empty of players. There was also a quirk with the various major boats and zeppelins dotted around the map, which were busted. Temporary portals were added to provide a workaround.

Industry observers note that "Thanks for everyone making this a great, super smooth launch," Greenfield wrote. "I’m going to head home and 'go to sleep' now. Yep, sleeping. Totally not playing WoW Forever until 3am. Nope.".

The reaction to this silky smooth launch has some players flabbergasted. "I can't believe how smooth this launch is" is the title of Reddit user Arizhela's post, at the moment topping the WoW Forever board. They continue: "I fully expected to not be able to play today, but I logged in with no queue and no lag.".

Sources indicate that another post, created in the early hours of this morning, is dubbed: "Never take a day off for launch, they said" in which a WoW player regrets not booking some time off from work this week, expecting problems. "You've been finessed son," replied user SnooWalruses3948, while SirePuns shared in the shock: "The advice was sound, but this time around the developers hired a witch I tell you. The code must’ve been witchcraft, the hardware must’ve been blessed by a witch as well.".

It is unclear just how well World of Warcraft: Forever's launch was, given the unsocialable and employment-averse release time in the dead of night for us Europeans, but it follows a record-breaking beta period in which many hopped back into the MMO. Impressions from this beta were largely positive, the magic of the old MMO seemingly recaptured.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Dark Lord has been upgraded from 'giant eyeball' (or sexy Sauron, if we're talking Rings of Power) to 'the galaxy's fastest hunk of junk', because now he's a Lego Millennium Falcon.

It has been revealed that posted to reddit by fan builder Minute_Food_2881, this alternate design takes the Lego Sauron's Helmet set (widely available at the usual suspects like Amazon) and reforges it into the most iconic ship in Star Wars. There's no cheating here; no extra pieces are used for this Lego Millennium Falcon beyond what's in the box. Considering how accurate and convincing the final product is, that makes this spin on one of the best Lego sets even more impressive - a bit like the fan-made Lego Navi set that's also doing the rounds this week.

In terms of the kit used for this build, the Dark Lord's signature helmet is a pretty manageable build; it's only 13 inches tall and 538 pieces. Because it's $69.97 via Amazon (a fraction of the price many Lord of the Rings sets reach), this is amongst the cheapest Lego options for fans of Middle-earth right now.

Sources indicate that thanks to the gray of Sauron's helmet along with its blend of sharp lines and curves, it translates surprisingly well to being a Millennium Falcon. Minute_Food_2881's design is instantly recognizable as Han Solo's ship as a result, and it's reminiscent of the official midi-scale Lego Millennium Falcon.

It has been revealed that the idea of turning something into Star Wars' most memorable bag of bolts is a long-running joke at this point (lovingly named "Can it Falcon?"), and there have been numerous amusing examples. It turns out that you can indeed turn a Lego pumpkin into the Millennium Falcon, for instance, and just last month someone made the ship from a chicken kit.

Industry observers note that not that the only cool sets from a galaxy far, far away are unofficial, of course. The new 50th anniversary Lego Star Wars sets are great, but I’m most interested in their weird collectible minifigures based on original concept art. Indeed, there are quite a few launching in January so it feels like 2027 could be a big one for fans of the franchise….

Because the franchise is celebrating a big birthday next year, there's plenty to get excited about; Hasbro goes back to the beginning with nostalgic Star Wars 50th anniversary action figures, for example.

I've been writing about games in one form or another since 2012, but these days you'll find me managing GamesRadar+'s tabletop gaming and toy coverage (I spend my time here handling everything from board game reviews to the latest Lego news). I've also been obsessed with Warhammer since the 1990s, and love nothing more than running tabletop RPGs like D&D as a Dungeon Master.

About a year ago, the devs behind Path of Exile 2 delayed the game's 1.0 release to an unspecified point in time, only offering the hope that it wouldn't slip into 2027 (doing much the same about half a year later). But there's good news: it won't! As the action RPG now has a 1.0 release date locked in, alongside a look at what you can expect when it arrives.

Recent findings suggest that as shared by developer Grinding Gear Games, Path of Exile 2 will be launching into 1.0 next month on December 11th. Probably the biggest aspect of the revision is the fact that the game's campaign will be completely playable, with the fifth and sixth acts being added in wrapping up the story that's been built up over its early access release. You'll also have two fresh classes to play around with, if you've gotten bored of the ones you've tried so far or just fancy something new.

According to recent reports, the first is the Shadow, which appropriately introduces a stealth mechanic. As you might expect of such a class, while you're in stealth, "monsters can't see you until you get within a short distance of them." Being in stated mode also bolsters your dagger with a range of bonuses, and the Shadow also has another weapon type available to them, traps. You prepare these in stealth, "then trigger them automatically as you strike. Traps explode in the order they were thrown, allowing you to set up the perfect combo!" And the other class is the Duelist, who has the new stance mechanic. This lets you strengthen your sword skills, "enhancing each of them in different ways," with various stances allowing for "even deadlier combinations.".

Beyond that, there's a upcoming league to try out that lets you team up with Varek and his mercs to "conquer Wraeclast!" A whole bunch of new items have been added in, with many being revamped, and you'll also find new skills gems and support gems reworked. The passive skill tree has also seen a makeover, and a number of classes have also received some improvements. You can read about all of that in more detail right here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that as part of today's (Thursday 5th November, 2026) financial results, Sony has confirmed that monthly active users, referred to as MAU, across both PlayStation 4 and 5, reached 127 million in September.
  • In Layman's terms, this simply means that more people are engaged with the PlayStation ecosystem now than ever before.
  • Industry observers note that notably, despite its mixed reception, Marvel's Wolverine was name-checked as a driving force for the decent performance over the past quarter - but that shouldn't be a surprise for anyone that's actually been paying attention to how the game performed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as part of today's (Thursday 5th November, 2026) financial results, Sony has confirmed that monthly active users, referred to as MAU, across both PlayStation 4 and 5, reached 127 million in September. This represents a seven percent growth year-on-year for the tech giant, and sets a fresh record high.

In Layman's terms, this simply means that more people are engaged with the PlayStation ecosystem now than ever before. And it's not just that there are more people using machines and occasionally booting up their consoles; active play time also increased over the past quarter, too, with total logged play time increasing by four percent, year-on-year. As a result, Sony and PlayStation noted that its Game & Network Services division saw revenue grow by nine percent year-on-year, resulting in operating profit rising by 83 percent year-on-year.

Industry observers note that notably, despite its mixed reception, Marvel's Wolverine was name-checked as a driving force for the decent performance over the past quarter - but that shouldn't be a surprise for anyone that's actually been paying attention to how the game performed. The game sold through 2.4 million copies as of 4th November (so, in roughly 50 days). Ghost of Yotei, meanwhile, has sold through 3.3 million since its launch in October 2025.

More people playing consoles, and for longer - it must all be good news for Sony right? Well, not all the graphs are showing growth. PS5 hardware sales continue to gradually decline: in the reporting period, Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 consoles, down from 4 million in the same quarter in 2025. But, with 100 million PS5 units out in the wild, and 127 million PlayStation accounts across the whole ecosystem, Sony doesn't seem that worried: instead, the company is now focusing on converting those with active accounts into more viable customers.

According to recent reports, elsewhere in the results, we heard from Sony CFO Lin Tao that the PlayStation 6 is on track and "progressing as scheduled", with "solid progress" expected on the machine in 2027. Regarding those falling PS5 sales, Tao also referenced that, and indicates it's all part of the natural cycle of console launches and iteration. "Although fresh PS5 unit sales are gradually declining as expected at this stage of the console life cycle, the PlayStation platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner," Tao explained. "[Next year,] we intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform.".

Recent findings suggest that it must be encouraging for Sony to see this growth in this quarter, especially after all the bad press and furore around the manufacturer's decision to end the manufacturing of PlayStation discs by January 2028. It seems to be a core part of the gaming audience's understanding of game ownership, the decision has been widely contested as anti-consumer. It's caused a lot of bad blood with PlayStation players over the past six months, but - seemingly, given these results - that has translated to very little material impact on Sony's bottom line.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, by this point I'm probably safe in assuming that you all know EA are shutting down BioWare, and that Mass Effect 5 has been cancelled in turn. You may have also seen that an internal trailer for Mass Effect 5, or Universe as it was seemingly going to be called, was leaked not long after the news broke, and that Sam Hulick, one of the composers on the original trilogy of games, shared he was going to offer up his re-scored version of the trailer. Well, it's N7 Day, as rough as that will be for many of the developers on the game, but Hulick has stood by his word, and shared an oral glimpse at what the world of Mass Effect Universe could have sounded like.

In a recent development, you can check out this new version of the trailer below, perhaps pop it on while you have a read of the rest of this post, as Hulick did also write in a Patreon blog about his experience with the series. "As part of my own closure, and as a love letter to the fans, I really wanted to re-score the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer in time for N7 Day this year," he wrote. "BioWare edited a killer track called “Quartz” by French 79 to fit their trailer, which I think hinted at a slight directional shift in the score. Using that as inspiration, along with the musical tone from my work on the first three Mass Effect games, I hit the studio and got to work.".

As it turns out, BioWare had actually reached out to Hulick asking him to potentially do some work for the project. "This year, BioWare emailed me asking if I was interested in working with them on an internal demo, and they stated they were 'hoping to get some music written that would feel like Mass [Effect], supporting our fresh direction.' Of course, I said yes!" This doesn't mean he wouldn't have composed the actual game, as a composer hadn't been officially selected, but Hulick said he was "more than happy to collaborate on the new game’s musical direction and help make their internal demo sound as good as it could.".

Industry observers note that hulick also spoke of some of the ideas he had for the direction Mass Effect Universe's soundtrack could take, noting how he "thought it would’ve been incredible to bring more songs with lyrics into the game," considering how many people loved the first game's end-credits song. "This would’ve been a great way to highlight more emotional moments in the narrative. Artists at the top of my collaboration list included Gunship, NINA, and The Midnight, all of whom have a moody, cinematic synthwave vibe that would’ve meshed well with the score in my head. And I’m pretty sure the Gunship guys are gamers, and if they’re Mass Effect fans, that would’ve been the icing on the cake!".

It has been revealed that of course, with the studio now closing, this never got to go very far, the news hitting Hulick "particularly hard, as the Mass Effect trilogy is a core part of my origin story as a composer." For the composer, ultimately "this trailer is my way of saying goodbye… at least for now." This continues to be a horrendously sad moment in the industry! As always, solidarity with the team at BioWare.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A stalwart of the Call of Duty franchise has fallen victim to layoffs at Activision. Having been at Treyarch for almost two decades, the now-former narrative dev revealed redundancies had occurred in a social media post.

Industry observers note that on LinkedIn, where many such changes are first revealed, Craig, a senior lead writer for Treyarch, thanked his colleagues for their long tenure at the studio. "After approximately 20 years at Treyarch, I was one of those affected by recent layoffs," he writes.

"I am proud and privileged to have worked alongside so many talented people - many of whom will remain friends for life - on so many amazing projects," he continues. "Thank you to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years.".

20 years at one tech giant is a strong shift, and Houston contributed to many Call of Duty releases in that time. He was a lead writer for a long period, before being promoted to senior lead in 2022.

Since it was at Treyarch, he primarily worked on the Black Ops series, shaping the campaigns of every single entry in that series thus far. He's contributed to Call of Duty more broadly, helping develop 2019's Modern Warfare and 2023's Modern Warfare 3.

Even if you're not a huge fan of Call of Duty, you've likely encountered his work if you enjoy comic book games. He was a producer of the X2: Wolverine's Revenge video game, and worked in the art department for Silver Surfer and Wolverine on the NES, and Spider-Man/X-Men: Arcade's Revenge on the SNES.

No further details of how sweeping the changes at Treyarch have been, but given the extensive nature of Xbox's restructuring, we could be hearing of quite a few more like Houston. Remember, Microsoft bought Activision-Blizzard in 2023, placing those devs on the chopping block amid the current reductions across the corporation's games division.

  • It has been revealed that county of Fortune just landed in early access a couple of days ago, and as mentioned (and as the name suggests), you're building up an entire county!
  • To start with, it's up to you where you want to place each of your settlements, deciding how they individually function as you do.

In a recent development, I know what you want. The humble city builder isn't enough for you any more, is it? You need a cities builder, you can't just stop at one, but you don't want to build up an entirely different city on a latest save file. If it were up to you, they'd all be on the same map, a motorway's worth of a drive away from each other. If we're talking contemporary cities, I can't help you, but if you can settle for numerous medieval towns across an entire county, then County of Fortune should do just fine.

It has been revealed that county of Fortune just landed in early access a couple of days ago, and as mentioned (and as the name suggests), you're building up an entire county! "You place whole settlements across the county and lay each one out on a medieval grid. Each one grows, specializes, and knits into a living region where rivers and resources decide what thrives," the game's Steam page explains. "As the county matures, a second game begins. Named mayors run each settlement. Rival noble houses weave politics across the region. And migrating cultures bless some villages, while complicating others.".

To start with, it's up to you where you want to place each of your settlements, deciding how they individually function as you do. The towns are then partially procedurally generated as they get built up, slowly connecting to other nearby towns. "The scale is the point. You are not zooming into a single town - you are zooming out to see a whole county come to life." A big part of the strategy comes down to how you navigate the map; finding resource deposits, picking appropriate terrain profiles, utilising rivers efficiently, finding a good climate, setting good trade routes, it's all about working with the land you've got.

Each settlement will produce different things depending on the materials available to them in close proximity, meaning each one has a unique function. You've got different types of characters to consider too: mayors, noble houses and cultures, all intersecting with different elements of how a town functions. Seems like a unique approach to city building! And as mentioned, it's out in early access; you can pick it up on Steam here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major revision, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

It has been revealed that first off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The upcoming update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

It has been revealed that our first upcoming arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

It has been revealed that keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

According to recent reports, evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent latest characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Recent findings suggest that evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

According to recent reports, you may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a fresh weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

According to recent reports, it can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this patch, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

According to recent reports, as part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a major expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 patch, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

Elsewhere, you’ll find latest items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 introduces and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, nintendo's latest financial earnings report is here, revealing healthy software sales thanks to the enormously popular Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream. Sales of Switch 2 hardware, however, are down.

As per Nintendo's 2nd Quarter fiscal earnings report, focusing on the three-month period ending 30th September 2026, Switch 2 hardware registered a significant drop in sales during the first half of the current financial year (FY27).

In a recent development, over that period, Nintendo sold 6.49m Switch 2 units and 1.27m units of the original Switch - equating to a 37.4 percent decline for Switch 2 and 32.7 percent decline for Switch 1 compared to the same period last year. Nintendo had previously forecast a decline in hardware sales, and the company still expects to sell 16.50m Switch 2 units by the end of the current fiscal year.

Nintendo software sales, on the other hand, saw a major year-on-year boost of 18.8 percent on Switch 2 (to 24.49m units) and a smaller increase of 6.8 percent on Switch 1. That's all thanks to the release of several popular first- and third-party titles over the first half of FY27. Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream was by far the most successful game with 8.81m units sold, followed by Rhythm Heaven Groove at 2.89m. Splatoon Raiders (the only Switch 2 exclusive of the three) sold 2.42m. Nintendo also highlighted a 60.5 percent year-on-year increase in digital game sales.

The increase in software unit sales and the "continued weakness of the Yen" couldn't prevent the overall business from declining by 15.3 percent year-on-year, however.

Other remaining releases in Nintendo' s current fiscal year include The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake (which releases today and was awarded five stars in Eurogamer's review), Switch 2 re-releases of Pikmin 2 and Xenoblade Chronicles 3, as well as Metroid Ravenous, which arrives early in 2027.
